title: Yoga
tagline: Union of body, mind, and spirit
description: Understand the core philosophy of yoga as a complete system for stilling the mind and reconnecting with your innermost self.

sutra.meaning: Now begins the discipline of Yoga. Maharishi Patanjali has gifted us his treatise on Yoga in a codified form.
sutra.wordMeanings: atha = now, auspicious beginning; yoga = union/discipline; anuśāsanam = teaching/exposition

sections.insight: This is a sacred beginning. When there is readiness the journey unfolds naturally.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Self-discipline is needed in areas which are not so pleasant to start with but give joy in the long term ie. Sattvic matters. Am I willing to persue the not so pleasant?
sections.practice: Find a quiet and comfortable place to sit and set a time for daily practice.
sections.meditation: Sit quietly and set an intention,3 min breath awareness and 10 min meditation.
sections.gurudevInsight: Discipline of YOGA Patanjali yoga sutras begins. Atha yoganushashanam Now, we will look into the discipline of Yoga. Now I will enunciate the discipline of Yoga. Shashana mean rules that somebody else puts on you. Anushashana is the rule that you put, impose on yourself.

sutra.meaning:
Yoga is the stilling of the fluctuations of the Consciousness ie Chitta. The Chitta comprises of the Manas, Buddhi, Ahamkar. The mind, intellect and ego.
Then the seer abides in their true nature.
sutra.wordMeanings: yogaḥ = yoga; citta = mind-stuff/consciousness; vṛtti = fluctuations/modifications; nirodhaḥ = restraint/cessation

sections.insight:
The mind keeps moving. Awareness—not suppression—brings stillness. Yoga shows us how. 
When the mind settles you experience your true self—peaceful and aware.
sections.reflectionPrompt: When is my mind most restless?
sections.practice: Observe thoughts without reacting. I should watch like I hawk which thoughts are frequent visitors.
sections.meditation:
3 min breathing. 
Pause and observe moments of stillness. meditate for 10 min

sections.gurudevInsight: There are certain vritis of the mind, which are problematic, which causes trouble; difficulties & certain others do not cause any difficulty. Pramanaviparyayavikalpanidrasmruti You call mind or consciousness or chitta – it’s all the same – different modes of consciousness. Five modes of Consciousness arises in your Self. Ya – I see this alps, mountains, water – all this, whatever you see now – these are the proof. Three types of pramana – Pratyaksha – anumana, agama. Our Mind constantly wants to have an obvious, solid experiential proof.

sutra.meaning:
Discipline in practice, self-study, study of the scriptures and surrender to God are the acts of yoga.
Yoga reduces suffering and prepares one for meditation.
sutra.wordMeanings: tapaḥ = austerity; svādhyāya = self-study; īśvara-praṇidhānāni = surrender to God; kriyā-yogaḥ = yoga of action

sections.insight: I need to be committed to make progress
sections.reflectionPrompt:
Can I make a commitment to myself?


Effort + awareness + surrender = growth.	Am I balanced in effort?
sections.meditation: 10 mins meditation with intention to be comitted
sections.gurudevInsight: This aspect sharpens the intellect, softens the mind, the heart. “Tapaswadhyayaishwarapranidhana kriyayoga” Sadhanapath means on practices, on the path. Action is part & parcel of this creation. There is activity in every thing in creation. Right from an atom, to the Sun, Moon & stars, there is activity. There is nothing that is stable in this creation or immobile, everything is very active.

sutra.meaning: Practice of yoga removes impurities and brings wisdom
sutra.padaVibhaga: yoga | aṅga | anuṣṭhānāt | aśuddhi | kṣaye | jñāna-dīptiḥ | ā | viveka-khyāteḥ
sutra.wordMeanings: yoga = yoga; aṅga = limbs; anuṣṭhānāt = from practice; aśuddhi = impurity; kṣaye = on destruction; jñāna-dīptiḥ = light of knowledge; ā = up to; viveka-khyāteḥ = discernment

sutra.meaning:
Eight limbs of yoga guide the path.
Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga
sutra.padaVibhaga: yama | niyama | āsana | prāṇāyāma | pratyāhāra | dhāraṇā | dhyāna | samādhayaḥ | aṣṭau | aṅgāni
sutra.wordMeanings: yama = restraints; niyama = observances; āsana = posture; prāṇāyāma = breath control; pratyāhāra = withdrawal; dhāraṇā = concentration; dhyāna = meditation; samādhayaḥ = absorption; aṣṭau = eight; aṅgāni = limbs

sections.gurudevInsight: A seed has the possibility that if it is not watered, then the possibility remains a possibility, it doesn’t manifest. Here patanjali steps in & says yogaangaanushthana - By practicing the limbs of yoga, by observing the limbs of Yoga, through yoga the impurities get eliminated & the viveka, the wisdom shines forth. The husk is gone, the sprout moves though it & comes up. They are (1) Yama (2) Niyama (3) Aasana (4) Pranayama (5) Pratyahara (6) Dhyana (7) Dharana (8) Samadhi. He goes into the details of each & what is the result that you can expect from each one of them. Yoga has 8 limbs, like a chair has got four legs, yoga has 8 limbs, or legs.
